sections.skill: Tell real government notices from look-alike paid offers

questions.prompt: What is a paid solicitation in this context?

choices.text: An offer designed to look official that charges a fee
A supplier invoice for goods the business received
A real tax bill from the IRS

questions.correct_answer: An offer designed to look official that charges a fee
questions.intro: New businesses receive official-looking letters. Some are real: tax agency notices, state filing reminders. Others are PAID SOLICITATIONS designed to look official, offering to file your annual report or provide a "certificate" for a large fee, or charging for things that are free, like an EIN from the IRS. Check the sender's name, look for small print saying "this is not a government agency," and verify by going to the official website or calling a number you find yourself. Never pay just because a letter looks urgent.
